title.said: three p p is the view. Where does the code go?

i1.said: This is Snake. The snake moves on its own, one square at a time. The arrow keys turn it.

i2.said: Eat the apple, and it grows. Hit a wall, and the game is over.

i3.said: We'll write this game three times, and each time, ask where the code should live.

i4.said: First, everything in one function. Then, a class that inherits from three p p. And last, the rules on their own.

t1.said: Version one. Everything is in main, like in our first app. And it works.

t2.said: Let's color each line by its job. Green lines are the rules of the game.

t4.said: In version one, they are all mixed together.

t5.said: Look at this line. To know if the snake has eaten, a rule asks a 3D shape where it is.

t6.said: So to test the rules, you need a window. And to change the picture, you have to touch the rules.

p1.said: Version two. A common first try is a Snake class that inherits from three p p's Group.

p2.said: A Group is a thing in three p p's 3D scene. So this says: the snake is a 3D scene object.

p3.said: But a snake is a piece of the game, not a scene object.

p4.said: It has a 3D look. And another class, Snake View, can own that look and draw it.

m1.said: Version three. The rules move into a class of their own, called Game.

m2.said: The snake's 3D look moves into another class, called Snake View.

m3.said: What's left stays in main. It sets up the window and the camera.

m4.said: And every step, main moves the game on, then asks the view to draw it.

g1.said: Game only knows squares on a grid. A view turns those squares into a picture.

g2.said: This view prints them as text, with no three p p at all. This one draws them in 3D, with three p p.

g3.said: One game, two pictures. The rules don't care who is watching.

b1.said: Game even gets a build of its own. Its C Make file doesn't mention three p p at all.

b2.said: Try to use three p p in it, and the build stops. The rules can't draw, not even by accident.

e1.said: And rules without a window are easy to test.

e2.said: Set up a snake next to an apple. Take one step. Check that the snake grew.

e3.said: It passes, without opening a single window.

z1.said: The rules live in Game, with no three p p. The 3D look lives in Snake View, and only the view uses three p p.

z2.said: Next time: who plays the game.
